conviction_note: Evidence is balanced. On the positive side are a subscriber-count floor in the company's own 6-K and strong SA new-vehicle sales. On the negative side, the Q2 EPS bar (ZAR9.72, +17% y/y) needs a step-up from Q1's +11% EPS growth, a guide raise looks unlikely, July's USD1.50 dividend will draw down the balance sheet, and the CEO has been selling. So p_up is 49 on an abs move of 9%. That abs move is rebuilt from the confirmed prints (Oct-25 about -12%, Jan-26 about +8%, May-26 -6.1%, Jul-26 +11.2%), not from the contaminated 1.86% baseline. The -0.2 impact_sum and the -0.18 scaled number agree in sign and size.

Company FY27 guide, reaffirmed 2026-07-15: Cartrack subscription revenue ZAR5,700-6,000m (+18-24%), Cartrack gross margin 70-72%, Cartrack operating margin 27-30%, EPS ZAR38.50-40.00 (+18-23%) (https://karooooo.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/KARO-Q1FY2027-SENS-20260716.pdf).
positioning_check: Short interest was 214,139 shares on the 2026-09-30 settlement: 2.74% of float, 2.3 days to cover, up 223% from 66,254 on 2026-09-15 (MarketBeat, https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NASDAQ/KARO/short-interest/). Spot $61.46 is -6.1% over 20 days and -10.6% from the 52-week high of $68.80. Insiders own about 75% of shares and the 20-day average volume is about 77k shares, so a thin float sets the reaction.

findings.finding: The company's 2026-10-05 6-K (Q2 date announcement) describes Karooooo as serving 'more than 2.9 million active subscribers', up from 'more than 2.8 million' in the Q1 release, when the actual count at May 31 was 2,804,694. That implies roughly 95k+ net adds between May 31 and early October, against the Q2 FY26 comparator of 70,740 net adds and Q1 FY27's record 142,472. The boilerplate is loose: in Oct-2025 it said '>2.5m' while the Q2 FY26 quarter-end was 2,456,989, so Q2 FY27 net adds could plausibly sit anywhere from about 55k to 145k. The read leans mildly toward Q2 net adds at or above last year's 70.7k.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Net adds drive this stock. Q2 FY26 net adds fell to 70,740 from 89,168 alongside an EPS miss, and the stock dropped about 12% the next day (Motley Fool 2025-10-15). Q1 FY27's record 142k net adds took it +11.2% (baseline 2026-07-15 amc).
findings.why_not_priced: The figure sits in boilerplate of a date-announcement 6-K that no aggregator parses. If the market had read it as strong, the stock would not have drifted -6% over 20 days into the print. It is weak evidence because the boilerplate rounds loosely.
findings.independence: Calibration comes from the company's own earlier boilerplate (Oct-2025 SENS, https://karooooo.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/KARO-HY26-Q2-SENS-20251015.pdf, '>2,500,000' against an actual 2,456,989). That is the same issuer's documents, not an independent source.

findings.finding: South African new-vehicle sales stayed strong through the quarter (June-August) and after it. NAAMSA reported August 2026 at 57,898 units (+11.4% y/y, the 23rd straight month of growth, LCVs +11.0%) and September at 61,645 (+12.7%). SA is about 76% of Cartrack subscribers (2,119,801 of 2,804,694), and SA net adds grew 92% y/y in Q1. This supports continued SA net-add momentum.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no history of the stock reacting to vehicle-sales data. Subscriber adds are the line it trades on (+11.2% Jul-26 on record adds; about -12% Oct-25 on slowing adds).
findings.why_not_priced: This is a broad public series, so it is mostly in the macro view. Transmission to Cartrack's net adds is unconfirmed by the company, which is why it is sized small. A market pricing a strong SA quarter would not have let the stock slip 6% in 20 days.
findings.independence: A different outlet carries the September figure: EWN 2026-10-04, https://www.ewn.co.za/2026/10/04/sas-new-car-sales-boom-continues-as-new-energy-vehicle-adoption-accelerates. This is a proxy, not a company number.

findings.finding: The Q2 EPS bar of ZAR9.72 implies +17% y/y against Q2 FY26 adjusted EPS of ZAR8.28. Q1 FY27 EPS grew only 11% (ZAR9.53 vs 8.55), and Cartrack's operating margin fell to 28% from 30%. Last year Q2 operating profit rose only about 1% q/q (ZAR352m to ZAR356m), and management said S&M 'will continue to increase for the remainder of FY2027'. Repeating last year's seasonal +1% q/q on Q1's ZAR410m operating profit gives about ZAR414m, roughly ZAR9.6 EPS at Q1's net/operating ratio. That is slightly under the bar, so there is a mild EPS-miss risk while revenue lands roughly in line.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: EPS misses have been sold: Q2 FY26 (Oct-25) EPS miss gave about -12%, Q4 FY26 (May-26) EPS miss gave -6.1%. EPS beats have been bought: Jan-26 +8%, Jul-26 +11.2%.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus sits mechanically on the FY guide's growth rate rather than on Q1's +11% EPS growth or last year's flat Q2 sequential operating profit. If the market doubted the bar, estimates would have been cut since July; none were found. This is an inference, and the bar is partly disputed ($0.589 vs $0.51), so it is capped small.
findings.independence: Last year's Q2 seasonality comes from the H1 FY26 SENS, https://karooooo.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/KARO-HY26-Q2-SENS-20251015.pdf. The S&M guidance comes from the Q1 6-K (https://karooooo.gcs-web.com/node/7166/html), which is the same release as the source.

findings.finding: FX translation: USD/ZAR averaged about 16.35 in Q2 (Jun-Aug) against about 16.61 in Q1, and about 17.65 at the Q2 FY26 translation point. The ZAR therefore stayed about 8% stronger y/y, the same headwind as Q1 (21% constant currency vs 19% reported), so this is not new. The Aug-31 convenience rate of about 16.15 sits below the roughly 16.44 implied by the $98.8m USD consensus, so an in-line ZAR1.624bn translates to about $100.6m, a mechanical +1.8% USD 'beat' in aggregator headlines.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No clean history. Q1's release headlined USD subscription revenue +32% against +19% in ZAR, and the stock rose 11.2%, but net adds were the driver.
findings.why_not_priced: Aggregator consensus in USD appears to have been struck at an older rate. Headline-driven US flow on a thin float can react to the USD print rather than the ZAR economics. The effect is small.
findings.independence: The translation convention (period-end H.10 rate) is stated in the Q1 SENS footnote, https://karooooo.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/KARO-Q1FY2027-SENS-20260716.pdf.

findings.finding: Q2 balance sheet: the USD1.50/share interim dividend (30.89m shares, about USD46m or about ZAR750m) was paid on 2026-07-20/27. At May 31, net cash was ZAR755m and Q1 free cash flow only ZAR60m, because IoT device investment rose to ZAR462m. Q2 should therefore show cash largely depleted or the ZAR750m overdraft (Capitec/Standard Bank) drawn, with lower interest income on the USD cash. Asked what the money buys: shareholder returns plus a funded subscriber ramp (record Q1 adds, IoT inventory up to ZAR524m), not distress.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print turned on the balance sheet. Q1's FCF collapse (ZAR60m vs ZAR338m) did not stop a +11.2% reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: The dividend is known, but the combination with weak FCF, which may produce a 'net debt' headline or lower interest income, is not in any preview found. It is mostly priced, hence sized small.
findings.independence: None from a different source; this is arithmetic on the same release.

findings.finding: Short interest rose 223% in two weeks, from 66,254 shares (2026-09-15) to 214,139 (2026-09-30), now 2.74% of float and 2.3 days to cover. The float is thin (about 77k shares/day, insiders about 75%) and there are no options. A building but uncrowded short adds squeeze fuel if the print is good and confirms bearish positioning if it is not.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Jul-26 good print moved +11.2% on this float. Prior short interest of 1-3 days to cover did not prevent -6% and -12% moves on misses.
findings.why_not_priced: FINRA data is public but is not in the sealed baseline. The level is too small to be a crowded-short mechanism, so it is sized small.
findings.independence: Earlier levels of 1.0-3.2 days to cover from Equibles/CurvedTrading (https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/karo/) show the September jump is unusual.

findings.finding: CEO and majority holder Isaias (Zak) Calisto sold in a steady series through August 2026, about 25.6k shares on Aug 4 at about $64.60, 33.8k on Aug 5 at about $66.14, 22.5k on Aug 10 at about $63.25 and smaller lots to Aug 26. findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Calisto's June-2025 USD75m secondary did not prevent subsequent beats from being bought (Jan-26 +8%).
findings.why_not_priced: The Form 4s are public. The steady post-print selling may be part of why the stock gave back the July gain, so it is mostly priced and sized near zero.
findings.independence: Separate Form 4 alerts on InsiderTrades, e.g. https://www.insidertrades.com/alerts/nasdaq-karo-insider-buying-and-selling-2026-08-25/. These are the same underlying filings.

findings.finding: A guide raise looks unlikely at H1. Q1 Cartrack subscription revenue of ZAR1,351m (+19%) sits in the lower half of the 18-24% FY range and needs ZAR1,450-1,550m a quarter for the rest of the year. Q1 EPS growth of +11% trails the guided +18-23%, gross margin is guided to contract to 70-72% (Q1 was 73%), and the guide 'assumes current FX rates' with the ZAR broadly unchanged since. The most likely outcome is a reaffirm, not the Jan-26-style raised outlook that bought +8%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Jan-26 raised revenue outlook gave +8%. Oct-25 reaffirm with an EPS miss gave about -12%. Jul-26 reaffirm with record adds gave +11.2%. A reaffirm on its own has not decided the sign.
findings.why_not_priced: Sell-side targets ($70-75, raised in July) imply momentum continues. If the market already expected only a reaffirm, the stock would likely have drifted further below the July close; it did drift -6%, so this is partly priced.
findings.independence: This uses the same document as finding 3 (Q1 SENS), but a different line (guidance vs the reported quarter). The Jan-26 raise precedent comes from https://www.fxleaders.com/news/2026/01/21/karooooo-q3-earnings-spark-share-price-jump-in-jse-kro-as-the-saas-growth-speeds-up/.
